product: Liberty Cyber Safe Insurance Policy (public wording)
clause: 1.A Liability arising out of loss of Personal/Corporate Information: The Insurer will pay to or on behalf of Insured all Damages and Defence Costs which arise out of a Claim by a Data Subject/Third Party against the Insured in respect of an actual or alleged Qualifying Breach of Personal/Corporate Information or the disclosure of Personal Information/Third Party Data by an employee of the Company.
question: If my company suffers a data breach exposing customer personal information and a third party sues us, is that covered?
gold_rationale: The Insurer will pay Damages and Defence Costs for a Claim arising from an actual or alleged Qualifying Breach of personal/corporate information, but the grant is subject to the Sublimit in the Schedule (item 6, 1.A) and the definition of a Qualifying Breach, so cover is conditional, not outright.
expected_citation: The Insurer will pay to or on behalf of Insured all Damages and Defence Costs

product: Liberty Cyber Safe Insurance Policy (public wording)
clause: 1.E Liability arising out of Company's Multimedia Activities: The Insurer will pay to or on behalf of Company all Damages and Defence Costs (not to exceed the Sublimit stated in item 6, 1.E of the Schedule) which arise out of a Claim by a Third Party against the Company solely in the performance of or failure to perform MultiMedia Activities arising from alleged or actual wrongful acts including defamation, libel, slander, or disparagement.
question: Are we covered if we are sued for defamation in digital content we published?
gold_rationale: Multimedia liability is a granted cover, but it is capped (not to exceed the Sublimit in item 6, 1.E of the Schedule) and limited to specified wrongful acts, so it is conditional on the sub-limit and the act falling within the module.
expected_citation: Liability arising out of Company's Multimedia Activities

question: Is a claim about an inaccurate product price description covered under the multimedia liability module?

product: Liberty Cyber Safe Insurance Policy (public wording)
clause: 2.B The Insurer will pay to the Company any Network Loss including Extra Expenses (not to exceed the Sublimit stated in item 6, 2.B of the Schedule) in respect of a Material Interruption that an Insured incurs after the Waiting Hours Period has expired and solely as a result of a Security Failure.
question: If a cyber-attack takes down our systems and we lose business income, is that covered?
gold_rationale: Network Loss / business interruption is covered only after the Waiting Hours Period has expired, solely as a result of a Security Failure, and up to the Sublimit in item 6, 2.B, so it is conditional on those triggers and the sub-limit.

question: Would we be covered for business interruption if a government seizes or destroys our servers?

product: Liberty Cyber Safe Insurance Policy (public wording)
clause: 5.37 Retention means the amounts specified as such in item 7 of the Schedule.
question: Is there an amount I have to bear myself before the cyber policy responds to a loss?
gold_rationale: The policy defines a Retention (the amount specified in item 7 of the Schedule) which the insured bears; the insurer responds only above that retention, so cover is conditional on the retention being met/exhausted.

product: Liberty Cyber Safe Insurance Policy (public wording)
clause: 10.3 Economic Sanctions: No insurer shall be deemed to provide cover and no insurer shall be liable to pay any claim or provide any benefit hereunder to the extent that the provision of such cover, payment of such claim or provision of such benefit would expose that insurer to any sanction, prohibition or restriction under United Nations resolutions or the trade or economic sanctions, laws or regulations of the European Union, Japan, United Kingdom, United States of America or any other Country imposing any such sanctions.
question: Will the policy pay a claim if doing so would breach international sanctions laws?
gold_rationale: Cover, claim payment and benefits are expressly excluded to the extent they would expose the insurer to UN/EU/UK/US or other sanctions, so a sanctions-breaching claim is not covered.

product: Liberty Cyber Safe Insurance Policy (public wording)
clause: Security Failure means a failure or intrusion in part or whole of the Computer System, including, without limitation, that which results in or fails to mitigate any Unauthorised access, unauthorised use, denial of service attack or receipt or transmission of a malicious code.
question: Does the policy cover losses caused by a denial-of-service attack?
gold_rationale: A denial of service attack is expressly included within the definition of Security Failure, which is the core trigger for the insuring modules, so losses from a DoS attack fall within cover (subject to the module triggers).
